objective: Make World Model verification identities reproducible from canonical state and semantic verification inputs, and replace fabricated verification timestamps with explicitly injected truthful wall-clock metadata.
decision_supported: Can identical verification inputs replay to the same stable verification identity while reporting truthful, explicitly classified timestamp metadata?
outputs: A World Model-internal validated verification context carrying the canonical state hash and truthful UTC wall-clock timestamp.
Stable SHA-256-based verification IDs derived from canonical semantic inputs.
Migrated World Model tests and the bounded scripted-demo producer.
Reproducibility, timestamp, invalid-input and integration evidence.
acceptance: Normal: the same run ID, task ID, canonical state hash, rule version, semantic result and ordered evidence references produce the same verification ID; covered by tests/unit/test_world_model_verification_identity.py.
Normal: two independent Python processes produce the same verification ID for identical inputs; covered by a subprocess test in tests/unit/test_world_model_verification_identity.py.

Normal: verification timestamps are supplied through an explicit context and emitted as truthful UTC wall-clock timestamps with clock_id=wall; covered by tests/unit/test_world_model_verification_identity.py.
Boundary: changing only verified_at does not change verification_id, although the emitted verified_at changes; covered by tests/unit/test_world_model_verification_identity.py.
Boundary: changing the canonical state hash changes verification_id; covered by tests/unit/test_world_model_verification_identity.py.
Boundary: changing evidence references or rule version changes verification identity; covered by tests/unit/test_world_model_verification_identity.py.

Boundary: evidence ordering used by the verifier remains deterministic and is represented in the identity material; covered by tests/unit/test_world_model_verification_identity.py and tests/unit/test_world_model.py.
Failure: malformed, blank, uppercase, truncated or non-hex canonical state hashes fail before a VerificationResult is returned; covered by tests/unit/test_world_model_verification_identity.py.
Failure: malformed, timezone-naive or non-UTC verification timestamps fail closed; covered by tests/unit/test_world_model_verification_identity.py.
Failure: monotonic clock metadata cannot be supplied for the RFC3339 wall-clock verified_at field; covered by tests/unit/test_world_model_verification_identity.py.

Regression: every public World Model verifier uses the shared identity and timestamp implementation while preserving existing status, reason, recovery and supporting-evidence behavior; covered by tests/unit/test_world_model.py.

Integration: demo_scripted obtains state_hash from create_world_state_snapshot over the exact persisted event stream and passes a real UTC verification context; covered by tests/integration/test_observe_plan_act.py.

Integration: scripted-demo output remains semantically reproducible without using verification wall time as causal ordering or freshness evidence; covered by tests/integration/test_observe_plan_act.py and the demo command.
Boundary: no interface schema or shared contract model is modified; proved by the fixed-base Task Packet boundary check and git diff evidence.
No test uses sleep or timing delays to establish correctness.

Pre-implementation red tests demonstrate that verifier output currently contains the fabricated 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z timestamp.

Focused test output proves state hash, evidence references and rule version affect verification identity.
Failure-test output proves malformed state hashes and clock metadata fail before result construction.
Integration-test capture proves demo_scripted supplies the state_hash generated from its persisted event stream.
Integration-test capture proves action verification remains based on observation evidence rather than fabricated timestamp metadata.
